title: TreatmentSelected.v1
description: A decision selected a treatment to execute (A§23). Emitted by decision-service — not by treatment-service — on `collections.treatment` keyed by `caseId`, in the same transaction as the `decision_audit` row and the `DecisionMade` event, so the intent to contact is durable before anything is dispatched. treatment-service consumes it, dedupes on the inbox key AND on a business `UNIQUE(decision_id)`, and runs the execution state machine (DEC-14); the two layers of dedupe are deliberate, because a topic-slice replay must produce zero duplicate dispatches (D§49). Emitted ONLY for ONLINE and BATCH decisions: SIMULATION and SHADOW runs never produce treatment events (D§40, A§87–88) — that is the boundary that keeps a strategy comparison from contacting real customers.

decisionId.description: The decision that selected this treatment. Also treatment-service's business idempotency key — `UNIQUE(decision_id)` on the treatment table means one decision can never produce two treatments, whatever the delivery semantics do.

caseId.description: Collection case the treatment belongs to, and the partition key of the event — treatments for one case are therefore strictly ordered, which is what stops two treatments racing on the same case. A treatment always has a case: a TREAT decision taken without one creates the case first.

accountId.description: Account being treated. Carried on the event so treatment-service never has to call back for it (A§7.3: no service reads another service's store).

customerId.description: Customer being contacted — the subject of the guardrail re-checks (do-not-contact, contact window, frequency caps) that treatment-service performs immediately before dispatch.

treatmentCode.description: The strategy's treatment code, e.g. `SMS_EARLY_REMINDER`. Identifies which `treatments[]` entry of the deciding strategy version was chosen.

type.description: Treatment kind. `CALL_TASK` is a work item for a human collector — dispatched as a case activity through the case API, not to a comms provider; the other four are automated sends handled by a channel adapter.

channel.description: Delivery channel, and the channel the execution guardrails (contact window, frequency cap, policy `FORBID_CHANNEL`) are evaluated against.

params.description: Channel/template parameters copied verbatim from the selected treatment in the strategy document, e.g. `{"templateId": "SMS_EARLY_1", "locale": "en-IE"}`. DELIBERATELY OPEN (`additionalProperties: true`), for the same reason as in strategy-document.v1.json: the key set belongs to the channel adapter and its message templates (DEC-15), which change on a provider's release schedule and must not force an event version. The adapter validates the parameters it requires at dispatch and fails the treatment with a reason code if one is missing. Never carries PII and never carries a decision input. May be an empty object.

allOf.title: treatment type ↔ channel mapping
allOf.description: The same closed 1:1 mapping as strategy-document.v1.json (SMS→SMS, EMAIL→EMAIL, LETTER→LETTER, CALL_TASK→CALL, DIGITAL→DIGITAL), enforced here too because this is the message a dispatcher acts on: an `SMS` treatment arriving on the `LETTER` channel must fail validation in the outbox, before the broker, rather than at a provider.
